idiom_name: scalafmt (.scalafmt.conf) with expression-oriented match/for instead of nested blocks
implementation_notes: Scala's accepted shape is whatever scalafmt produces from .scalafmt.conf, and the language style guide governs which braces may be omitted, so formatting is a checked-in configuration rather than a hand discipline. The depth story differs from the imperative languages: return is not idiomatic - inside a closure it compiles to a NonLocalReturnControl throw - so the flattening tool is expression-oriented style, where match, for-comprehensions and Option combinators hold one indentation level where an imperative language would nest. The classic brace form is still right for multi-statement bodies and for while loops, where the style guide requires braces.
code_sketch:
def depth(node: Node): Int = node match {
  case Leaf                => 1
  case Branch(left, right) =>
    val dl = depth(left)
    val dr = depth(right)
    1 + math.max(dl, dr)     // one level, no early return
}
pitfalls: return inside a closure compiles to a NonLocalReturnControl exception and can silently do nothing when the closure runs on another thread; flatten with match or for instead of porting the imperative guard style.
Brace-omission rules interact with scalafmt's indent settings; changing them reformats the codebase, so pin the scalafmt version in .scalafmt.conf and format in CI.
Partial functions passed as arguments ('{ case ... }') indent inside the call and read as a nesting level; extract them into named values when they grow.
